title: Substrate truth — decompose moneta_available() into its five claims
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). All oracle conditions met and measured. The leg ALSO refutes three of its own brief's premises and repairs one live Law-3 defect it found on the seam the brief told it to reuse. Nothing pushed, merged or tagged.

oracle.evidence: available / version / file / schema_registered / schema_in_use all present, each schema field paired with a *_reason. pxr blocked on the meta path in a clean subprocess -> both report None with 'could not check: pxr unavailable', no traceback.

oracle.condition: the positive control DEMONSTRATED: check fires with PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME unset
oracle.evidence: Two-sided, subprocess-isolated, on BOTH interpreters. unset -> False; PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME=<Moneta>/schema -> True. A third pin asserts the two arms DISAGREE, so a check insensitive to the only input that determines the answer cannot pass.

oracle.condition: no raise path added to _make_store or any import path
oracle.verdict: MET — and one PRE-EXISTING raise path was CLOSED

oracle.condition: gate suite holds at 4881+ with 0 failed

five_conditions_measured.headline: moneta_available() returns True on both interpreters while four of the five conditions are false or unreachable.

positive_control._method: subprocess.run with a fresh interpreter per arm, PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME the only variable. USD plugin registration is process-global; an in-process set-and-requery does NOT change the answer (observed while writing the pins) and would contaminate every sibling test. Reuses Moneta's own tests/_schema_gate_subprocess.py pattern rather than reinventing it.

arms.detail: resolves; props = attendedCount, lastEvaluated, payload, priorState, protectedFloor, utility

positive_control.verdict: DEMONSTRATED on both interpreters. The check discriminates; it is not a decoration.
positive_control.corroborating_observation: Same authored bytes, both arms: with the path unset a prim reports GetTypeName()=='MonetaMemory' while IsA(Usd.Typed) is False and its prim definition is EMPTY. With it set, both flip True. That is the dead-bytes cell, live.

findings.claim: The brief's premise is stale. Memory prims are authored TYPED today, not as untyped `def`. usd_target.py sets prim_spec.typeName = 'MonetaMemory' unconditionally, in BOTH Moneta copies.
findings.contradicts: harness/prompts/h6.md:22 and R64, both citing DEEP_THINK_BRIEF_codeless_schema.md:15. That brief describes v1.1.0, pre-surgery; the migration landed and the brief was never updated.
findings.note: The brief anticipated this: 'If prims ARE typed, that is a finding and the brief is stale.'

findings.claim: R64's predicted live state — registered=True, in_use=False — does not reproduce. schema_registered is FALSE on both interpreters in the default environment.
findings.anchor: packages/synapse.json (sets SYNAPSE_ROOT, PYTHONPATH, MONETA_SRC, SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND — and NOT PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME); C:/Users/User/Moneta/SURGERY_complete_codeless_schema.md:21 ('The substrate does not register the plugin itself')
findings.detail: Nothing in SYNAPSE's Houdini package and nothing in Moneta ever sets PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME. Registration only happens when an operator sets it by hand. The cell that looks like success on THIS build is therefore the inverse of the one R64 named: !registered && in_use — a typeName on disk the runtime cannot resolve.
findings.consequence: Both cells are handled by the shipped doctor check; neither can report ok.

findings.claim: SYNAPSE authors ZERO USD through Moneta. Conditions 4 and 5 are not half-migrated — they are structurally unreachable on SYNAPSE's live path.
findings.anchor: python/synapse/memory/moneta_store.py:215-227 builds MonetaConfig without use_real_usd; C:/Users/User/Moneta/src/moneta/api.py:136 defaults use_real_usd=False; api.py:255-268 selects MockUsdTarget on that default
findings.detail: Live probe: MonetaBackedStore.from_storage_dir(...) -> handle.authoring_target is MockUsdTarget, config.use_real_usd is False, and walking the store dir after a deposit + save finds zero .usd/.usda/.usdc files. Measured on both interpreters.
findings.consequence: 'Moneta is SYNAPSE's USD substrate' is true of the ECS and false of the USD layer. schema_in_use() reports None (UNKNOWN) with that wiring named in its reason string, rather than False — reporting False would read as 'we looked at the prims and they are untyped', which is not what happened.

findings.claim: store.py's `except ImportError` arm was DEAD CODE, and the surviving arm reported the exact inverse of the truth. Law 3 violation on the precise seam the brief instructed this leg to reuse.
findings.detail: moneta_store imports nothing from moneta at module scope, so `from .moneta_store import MonetaBackedStore` ALWAYS succeeds; from_storage_dir then raises RuntimeError, never ImportError. Every Moneta-absent seat fell through to the ERROR arm and was told the backend 'is installed but failed to initialize ... This is an API-drift or defect, not a missing dependency' — for a package that was simply not installed.
findings.proof: Clean interpreter with moneta blocked on the meta path: import of moneta_store SUCCEEDED, from_storage_dir raised RuntimeError, and _make_store emitted the inverted ERROR. After the fix the same probe emits WARNING 'Moneta is not importable ... falling back to jsonl'.
findings.status: REPAIRED in this leg. Both arms are now reachable and both are pinned; M12/M13/M14 fire.
findings.note: Found independently by the concurrent session (H6-F7) and re-verified here by my own probe rather than taken on report.

findings.claim: schema_in_use is NOT evidence of a working substrate on its own. Sdf authoring is schema-blind: typeName is written to disk with or without a registered schema.
findings.anchor: C:/Users/User/Moneta/tests/_schema_gate_subprocess.py:34-54 (Moneta's own false-positive defense); measured here on both interpreters
findings.detail: PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME unset: GetTypeName()=='MonetaMemory', IsA(Usd.Typed)==False, GetPrimDefinition().GetPropertyNames() empty. Set: both True and the definition is populated.
findings.consequence: The registered/in_use PAIR is the unit of truth, not either field. The doctor check refuses ok unless both are demonstrated, and the dead-bytes cell is named explicitly.

findings.claim: Condition 2 confirmed false — with a refinement LEDGER.F1 did not carry. The two interpreters load different COPIES, but the sources are byte-equivalent apart from line endings and one docstring line.
findings.anchor: diff of C:/Python314/Lib/site-packages/moneta vs C:/Users/User/Moneta/src/moneta, normalized for CRLF
findings.detail: Only two files differ raw: attention_log.py (CRLF only — identical after normalization) and usd_target.py (identical except one removed docstring line referencing docs/patent-evidence/pass5-usd-threadsafety-review.md). Identity/provenance diverge (pip 1.2.0rc1 vs worktree 2965e5d with 2 untracked files, version None); behaviour does not — today.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Different copies' alone overstates today's behavioural risk and understates the governance risk: nothing keeps them in sync, and the shipping side is a live working directory. The discriminating field is `file`, not `version`.
findings.adjacent: MONETA_SRC pinning is LEDGER's lane, not this leg's. Not touched.

findings.claim: Article V was violated on this leg: TWO independent sessions executed harness/prompts/h6.md against this one worktree and branch concurrently, and both held write tools.
findings.detail: For roughly three minutes python/synapse/memory/moneta_runtime.py carried two competing implementations; Python binds the last definition, so one silently shadowed the other. The second session detected it, backed its own block out byte-exactly, preserved it at <its scratchpad>/h6_orchestrator_block.py, wrote no test and no commit, filed the ticket and STOPPED — which is the correct behaviour and is why this leg is recoverable.
findings.observable_symptom: This session's first pin run reported 7 failures and the immediately-following identical run reported 3. That was not test flakiness; it was a concurrent writer. Recorded because 'flaky test' was the wrong diagnosis and would have sent the leg down a false trail.
findings.integrity_check_after: ast.parse clean on all four touched files; zero duplicate top-level definitions in moneta_runtime.py (398 lines, 10 defs) and doctor.py (713 lines, 20 defs); the surviving implementation is the one whose pins and 14-mutation battery are recorded here. No writes from the other session after 16:27:07.
findings.disposition: The other session's recon is preserved verbatim in the ticket and is NOT deleted (Law 4). Its findings were re-derived independently here rather than inherited; F4 is the one it surfaced first, and it was re-proven by probe before being acted on.

changes.what: schema_registered() and schema_in_use(usd_root=None) as TRI-STATE checks (True/False/None) with paired reason strings; moneta_provenance(usd_root=None) folds both in and is fully fenced. SCHEMA_TYPE_NAME / USD_ROOT_FILENAME / traversal cap are named constants. Module docstring carries the five conditions and the dead-bytes measurement.
design_notes: NOT cached — a cache cannot observe a subprocess that sets PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME, which is the only honest way to test registration.
Composes the stage (Usd.Stage.Open) rather than reading the root layer, because Moneta routes memory prims into sublayers.

Both checks are independent of moneta_available(): registration is a property of the USD runtime, not of whether the Python package imports. Gating on `available` would re-collapse two of the five conditions into one.

changes.what: H6-F4 repair — ask moneta_available() instead of inferring absence from an exception type, so both arms are reachable and neither lies; and fence the provenance lookup inside the ERROR handler so it cannot escape _make_store.

_check_moneta_substrate — every (registered, in_use) cell gets a verdict; only True/True can report ok; both look-like-success cells fail and say why; skipped when the Moneta backend is not selected on this seat. Wired into run_doctor.
tri-state contract, two-sided subprocess positive control, four reader controls, dead-bytes behaviour, no-raise contract on the startup path, F4 both-arms pins, and an 8-cell doctor table.

for_ruling.topic: R64 and harness/prompts/h6.md:24 predict a live state that does not reproduce
for_ruling.detail: Both assert `registered=True, in_use=False`. Live is `registered=False` on both interpreters, and for SYNAPSE `in_use` is UNKNOWN because no USD is authored at all. The brief anticipated exactly this contingency and asked for it to be surfaced.
for_ruling.ask: Amend R64 and h6.md to the measured state, and mark DEEP_THINK_BRIEF_codeless_schema.md:15 stale in Moneta. Article VII: amendments commit before the work they govern.
for_ruling.agent_position: Evidence, not a decision. The measurement is in five_conditions_measured with its producer named.

for_ruling.topic: Should SYNAPSE's Moneta store author real USD? (H6-F3)
for_ruling.detail: from_storage_dir builds MonetaConfig without use_real_usd=True, so the live handle is MockUsdTarget-backed and conditions 4 and 5 cannot be true regardless of the schema migration.
options: Leave as-is. Moneta serves as an in-memory ECS with snapshot durability. Cheapest, and today's behaviour. But 'Moneta is SYNAPSE's USD substrate' remains false at the USD layer and should stop being claimed.

Set use_real_usd=True with usd_target_path under <storage_dir>/.moneta. Makes conditions 4 and 5 reachable and memory legible in usdview. Costs: real disk I/O per sleep pass, a new on-disk layout to version and back up, and a durability surface that has never run under SYNAPSE's load.
for_ruling.agent_position: Out of this leg's scope — it is a product direction call (Article I). The field reports UNKNOWN with the wiring named, so the gap is visible rather than silently false either way.

for_ruling.topic: Should the Houdini package set PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME? (H6-F2)
for_ruling.detail: Registration is process-global and must be in the package env — setting it at runtime provably does not work (observed: setting it after pxr load leaves the registry unchanged). Nothing sets it today, by Moneta's deliberate design.
options: Do not set it. Typed prims stay dead bytes wherever they are authored, and condition 3 stays false. Honest, and now visible in the doctor.

Add it to packages/synapse.json. Makes condition 3 true and prims legible in usdview. Cost: SYNAPSE injects a USD plugin path into every Houdini session on the seat, which affects global plugin resolution for work unrelated to SYNAPSE.
for_ruling.agent_position: Recommend deciding this together with FR-2 — registering a schema nothing authors buys nothing, and authoring typed prims without registering it produces exactly the dead-bytes cell.

for_ruling.topic: moneta_substrate returns fail on a deployed seat; check_doctor is green only when summary.fail == 0
for_ruling.detail: The fail is true. Softening it to keep a gate green would destroy the instrument this leg exists to build (Law 7). But it does mean a deployed-seat doctor run is red until FR-2/FR-3 are decided.
for_ruling.ask: Confirm the truthful fail stands, or rule that an un-remediated-by-design condition should report differently.
for_ruling.agent_position: Shipped as fail. Not softened. Noting that check_doctor is already red for an unrelated pre-existing reason, so this changes the count, not the colour.

for_ruling.topic: Two sessions ran H6 in one worktree (H6-F7) — Article V, structurally
for_ruling.detail: The .claude/.orch_launched marker existed and was not honoured as a lock. Both runs held write tools. Recovery worked only because the second session voluntarily stopped; nothing enforced it. This is the same shape as R61: enforcement in the definition, not the instruction.
for_ruling.ask: Should the orchestrator refuse to dispatch a leg whose worktree already carries a live .orch_launched marker, and should an interactive session be given the same interlock?
for_ruling.agent_position: Recommend yes and treat it as a harness fix, not a per-leg discipline. Also worth recording: the collision presented as a flaky test (7 failures then 3 on identical consecutive runs). 'Flaky' was the wrong diagnosis and would have wasted the leg.

for_ruling.topic: The shadow backend branch has the same shape as the F4 defect
for_ruling.detail: store.py's `shadow` branch catches bare Exception and logs a single WARNING, so not-installed and installed-but-broken are indistinguishable there too.
for_ruling.ask: Fold into a follow-on, or leave.
for_ruling.agent_position: Not touched — outside this brief's named scope, and it does not currently claim a distinction it fails to make (unlike the moneta branch, which did). Flagged so it is not lost.
